paragraphs.source_en: The excavations undertaken in the Central Sahara bring very unequal amounts of information for the respective mountainous regions. While in the Tassili n'Ajjer only one site, Tin Hanakaten, was systematically excavated (Aumassip 1980-1), in the Algerian Tadrart no excavation has been carried out. In the Acacus nine shelters were excavated, namely Tin Torha North, Tin Torha East, Tin Torha Two Caves, Uan Muhuggiag, Uan Tabu, Uan Telocat, Uan Afuda, Fozzigiaren and Imenennaden, and a large surrounding area was submitted to a geoarchaeological survey (Barich 1978; Cremaschi & Di Lernia 1998; Mori 2000). Thus, we have a very poor knowledge about the archaeology in the Algerian region of the rock art whereas in the Libyan area the prehistoric situation is well documented.

paragraphs.source_en: The archaeological record is very similar not only between shelters in the Acacus but also in the excavated shelter in the Tassili. Uan Afuda shelter in the Acacus was excavated by Cremaschi, Di Lernia (1995, 1996b, 1996c) and Garcea (1995). The lowest stratigraphic layer, composed of aeolian sand, testifies a Late Pleistocene human occupation of the massif even during the worst climatic periods. A few unweathered Middle Palaeolithic artefacts were dated between 90,000 and 69,000 BP (Di Lernia 1999). These are separated from Holocene sediments by about a meter of aeolian sand, sterile from an archaeological point of view, and interpreted as a hiatus in human occupation.

paragraphs.source_en: Groups of Epipalaeolithic hunter-gatherers reoccupied the cave at the very beginning of the Holocene, at 9,765+105 BP (calBP 11,096+179). Microlithic industry features high quality raw material, such as local quartz and quartzite. Flint of good quality, even if particularly rare, is always present in the Early Holocene occupations of the area, but outcrops of flint are located hundreds of kilometres apart, which suggest that these groups were highly mobile (Di Lernia 1999). There is a simple structure in the form of an alignment of stones, possibly a stonewall used as a windbreak, dated at 9,260+290 BP (calBP 10,508±429).
